business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K Item 1 Business and Item 7 MD&A.
business_model.claim: Slide is a coastal specialty P&C insurer that writes single family, condominium, and commercial residential policies in coastal states along the Atlantic seaboard.
quotes: We focus on profitable underwriting of single family, condominium and commercial residential policies in the property and casualty (P&C) industry in coastal states along the Atlantic seaboard through our insurance subsidiary, Slide Insurance Company ("SIC").

business_model.claim: The company operates as one reportable segment.
quotes: We have one reportable segment.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K and 10-Q MD&A.
business_model.claim: Gross premiums written are the primary revenue driver, composed of assumed premiums from Citizens policy assumptions, block acquisitions from third-party insurers, renewals of existing policies, and new business written through independent agents and the DTC channel.
quotes: Gross premiums written represent, with respect to a fiscal period, the sum of assumed premiums written from Citizens policy assumptions (net of opt-outs) plus direct premiums written (premiums from subsequent renewals of such Citizens policies and new and renewal policies written through independent agents and our DTC channel, net of any midterm cancellations), in each case prior to amounts ceded to reinsurers.

business_model.claim: In 2026 the company assumed 47,718 policies representing approximately $102.5 million in assumed unearned premiums from Citizens, which carry no upfront acquisition costs.
quotes: In 2026 we assumed 47,718 policies, representing approximately $102.5 million in assumed unearned premiums from Citizens. These policies carry no upfront acquisition costs and are captured in our current treaty year reinsurance program.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A; figures from the 10-Q income statement.
business_model.claim: Net investment income is a secondary revenue source, generated from interest on cash, fixed-maturity securities, money market accounts, and other investments, plus realized gains or losses.
quotes: Net investment income represents interest earned from cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash, fixed-maturity securities, money market accounts and other investments and the realized gains or losses from the sale of investments.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K and 10-Q MD&A.
business_model.claim: Florida law allows insurers to charge policyholders a $25 policy fee on each policy written, recognized as income immediately upon collection under ASC 606.
quotes: Florida law allows insurers to charge policyholders a $25 policy fee on each policy written. Policy fees represent such upfront policy fees. These fees are not subject to refund, and accordingly we recognize policy fees as income immediately when collected in accordance with ASC 606

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K and 10-Q MD&A.
business_model.claim: Losses and loss adjustment expenses incurred, net are the largest expense line, reflecting losses paid, claims resolution expenses (adjusters, attorneys, investigators), and changes in reserves for unpaid losses, in each case net of losses ceded to reinsurers.
quotes: Losses and loss adjustment expenses incurred, net reflect losses paid, expenses paid to resolve claims, such as fees paid to adjusters, attorneys and investigators, and changes in our reserves for unpaid losses and loss adjustment expenses incurred, net during the fiscal period, in each case net of losses ceded to reinsurers.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K Item 1 Business – Reinsurance section.
business_model.claim: Reinsurance premiums paid to reinsurers is the single largest cost of the company, purchased to limit exposure to catastrophic events such as hurricanes.
quotes: Reinsurance is an important part of our risk management strategy and premiums paid to reinsurers is our single largest cost.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K and 10-Q MD&A.
business_model.claim: Policy acquisition and other underwriting expenses consist of commissions paid to outside agents at policy issuance, premium taxes, and inspection fees; Citizens-assumed policies carry no such costs until renewed.
quotes: Policy acquisition and other underwriting expenses consist of the following items: (i) commissions paid to outside agents at the time of policy issuance, (ii) premium taxes and (iii) inspection fees.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K Item 1 Business – Distribution section.
business_model.claim: The company distributes policies through two channels: independent agents and direct-to-consumer (DTC), with the DTC channel focused on low-cost acquisition through embedded relationships with mortgage bankers and trade organizations.
quotes: We market and write insurance policies through two channels: our independent agents and DTC.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K Item 1 Business – Technology section.
business_model.claim: The company's proprietary technology, backed by an approximately $8.9 trillion TIV underwriting and claims dataset, enables real-time policy-level profitability assessment and prospective reinsurance cost estimation at the point of sale.
quotes: Our underwriting technology has been an important component of our success and is backed by our proprietary approximately $8.9 trillion TIV underwriting and claims dataset, which provides us with real-time intelligence to drive superior decision making.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 8-K earnings release.
business_model.claim: The Q3 2026 combined ratio of 59.3% reflected $34.2 million of catastrophe losses from convective storms in Florida, while the accident-year loss ratio (excluding catastrophe losses and prior-period development) improved to 25.5% from 27.5% in the prior-year period.

competitive_position.claim: Slide positions itself as a technology-enabled coastal specialty insurer targeting underserved single-family, condominium, and commercial residential markets along the Atlantic seaboard, exploiting capacity withdrawn by larger national carriers.

Coastal specialty market demand for insurance products has increased over the last few years as the larger, national insurance carriers have reduced their underwriting capacity in such markets which has created a unique market opportunity for us to capitalize on the imbalance of supply and demand.

Slide Insurance Holdings, Inc. ("Slide" or the "Company") (Nasdaq: SLDE) announced today that its Board of Directors ("Board") has approved the initiation of a quarterly dividend of $0.07 per common share.

material_events.basis: stated in the cited item (8-K earnings release, Exhibit 99.1, filed October 29, 2026)
material_events.claim: Slide raised its full-year 2026 guidance, increasing the lower end of gross written premiums to a range of $1.90 billion to $1.95 billion (from $1.85 billion to $1.95 billion) and raising full-year net income expectations to $500 million to $520 million (from $455 million to $470 million), inclusive of up to $50 million of pre-tax losses related to Hurricane Isaias in Q4.
quotes: The Company raised the lower end of its gross written premiums range and now expects to generate full year gross written premiums in the range of $1.90 billion to $1.95 billion, compared to its prior range of $1.85 billion to $1.95 billion.

The Company also raised its expectations to generate full year net income in the range of $500 million to $520 million, compared to its prior range of $455 million to $470 million, which will result in return on equity above 40% for the full year. The Company's updated range is inclusive of up to $50 million of pre-tax losses related to Hurricane Isaias in the fourth quarter.

risks.basis: Stated in P1 (10-K Item 1 Business, Reinsurance section) and P2 (10-K Item 1A Risk Factors); the expiration dates are explicit, the renewal risk language is the company's own disclosure
risks.claim: Slide's catastrophe reinsurance agreements expired May 31, 2026 and catastrophe bonds mature between April 24, 2026 and June 1, 2028, creating a renewal window in which the company could face higher costs, reduced limits, or unavailable capacity.
quotes: Our current catastrophe reinsurance agreements excluding catastrophe bonds expire on May 31, 2026, with catastrophe bonds maturing between April 24, 2026, and June 1, 2028; other agreements are continuous or expire on specified dates such as November 1, 2026.

We may be unable to renew or replace expiring treaties on comparable terms, limits, or pricing, or at all, which could force us to retain more risk, reduce underwriting volume, or incur higher reinsurance costs that pressure profitability until premium rates can be adjusted, subject to regulatory approval.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 (risk factor language), P3 (2025 10-K MD&A), and P4 (Q3 2026 10-Q MD&A); the policy counts and dollar amounts are explicitly disclosed
risks.claim: Slide's growth thesis partly depends on the Florida Citizens Property Insurance Corporation depopulation program, which provided 191,850 assumed policies in 2025 but only 47,718 in the first nine months of 2026, and the company warns there is no assurance the program will continue.
quotes: There can be no assurance that Citizens will decide to continue the depopulation program for a significant period of time, or at all.
In 2025 we assumed 191,850 policies, representing approximately $373 million in assumed unearned premiums from Citizens.
In 2026 we assumed 47,718 policies, representing approximately $102.5 million in assumed unearned premiums from Citizens.

risks.basis: Stated in P6 (8-K earnings release, October 27, 2026) and P4 (Q3 2026 10-Q MD&A); the cat loss figure, Isaias provision, and guidance range are explicit company disclosures
risks.claim: Q3 2026 already absorbed $34.2 million in catastrophe losses from Florida convective storms, and the company's raised full-year net income guidance of $500–$520 million is inclusive of up to $50 million of pre-tax losses from Hurricane Isaias in Q4 2026, meaning a single additional severe event could materially exceed guidance.
quotes: Losses and loss adjustment expenses (LAE) incurred, net were $101.3 million, which included $34.2 million of catastrophe losses from convective storms in Florida in the quarter and $18.0 million of favorable prior period reserve development.
The Company's updated range is inclusive of up to $50 million of pre-tax losses related to Hurricane Isaias in the fourth quarter.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 (10-K risk factors) and P6 (8-K earnings release); the reserve balance is from F1 (10-Q balance sheet, table in thousands)
risks.claim: Slide carries $503.870 million (in thousands) in loss and loss adjustment expense reserves as of September 30, 2026, and the company explicitly warns that actual incurred losses may exceed these reserves, which would require a reserve strengthening that reduces net income and shareholders' equity in the period identified.
quotes: Our actual incurred losses may be greater than our loss and loss adjustment expense reserves, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition.

If any of our insurance reserves should prove to be inadequate for the reasons discussed above, or for any other reason, we would be required to increase reserves, which may negatively affect our net income and shareholders' equity in the period in which the deficiency is identified.
